pathway.title: Embecta Corp. — Full credit assessment
pathway.question: Should we own this issuer, in which instrument, and why?

runs.text: The core business is losing price and volume in the United States, and that is where the earnings come from. United States revenue fell 20.6% in nine months 2026 and pen needle revenue fell 13.2%, while group revenue lost USD 60.0 million to volume and USD 27.4 million to price against nine-month revenue of USD 816.4 million a year earlier. Cost of products sold rose to USD 311.9 million from USD 298.1 million while revenue fell, so price concessions went straight to gross profit and gross margin dropped to 58.7% from 63.5%. Management attributes the shortfall to competition and soft market volumes and assumes both continue for the rest of the year, so the erosion should be read as the base case, not a one-quarter event. Basis: EX99.1_2026-06-30_embc_q32026ex-991-htm.htm.jsonl, pages 2–4; 10-Q_2026-06-30_embc.htm.jsonl, page 34; EX99.1_2026-03-31_embc_q22026ex-991-htm.htm.jsonl, page 2; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C9; calculation C10

Management's raised margin guidance still implies a weaker fourth quarter than the third. Fiscal 2026 revenue guidance of USD 1,015 million to USD 1,035 million implies fourth-quarter revenue of USD 260.3 million to USD 280.3 million against USD 271.7 million in the third quarter, and adjusted operating margin guidance of 23.50% to 24.00%, with adjusted revenue equal to reported revenue as in every reported period, implies fourth-quarter adjusted operating income of USD 41.2 million to USD 51.1 million against USD 69.4 million in the third quarter. The documents do not explain the step-down, which is either caution or a heavier fourth quarter, so the third-quarter run rate should not be annualised. Basis: EX99.1_2026-06-30_embc_q32026ex-991-htm.htm.jsonl, pages 1–2; EX99.1_2026-06-30_embc_q32026ex-991-htm.htm.jsonl, pages 4–5; calculation C12

Cash flow is the main support, but it has been volatile and is partly funded by receivable sales. Free cash flow of USD 164.6 million over the last twelve months is 61.9% of reported EBITDA and capital expenditure is only 0.9% of revenue, so there is a real source of debt service. The record is less steady: free cash flow was USD 41.2 million, USD 19.9 million and USD 182.4 million in fiscal 2023, 2024 and 2025, and nine-month free cash flow fell to USD 87.9 million from USD 105.7 million. In nine months 2026 USD 167.2 million of trade receivables, 22.2% of revenue, were sold to a third party on an uncommitted basis, 2.6 times the USD 63.2 million sold in all of fiscal 2025, so part of operating cash flow depends on a buyer that can stop purchasing; the outstanding sold balance is not established. Basis: 10-K_2025-09-30_embc.htm.jsonl, pages 103, 135; 10-Q_2026-06-30_embc.htm.jsonl, page 4; 10-Q_2026-06-30_embc.htm.jsonl, page 25; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C2; calculation C3

Leverage has turned up while the covenant path asks for the opposite. Net debt rose USD 67.7 million to USD 1,240.4 million between 2025-09-30 and 2026-06-30 while last-twelve-months reported EBITDA fell to USD 265.8 million from USD 284.3 million, taking net leverage to 4.67x from 4.12x; pro forma for the dividend payable on 2026-09-15 the figures are USD 1,241.0 million and 4.67x. The amended revolver tests a first lien net leverage ratio of at most 4.75x through 2027-06-30 that steps down to 3.75x from 2028-04-01, and an interest coverage ratio of at least 2.50x that steps up to 3.00x from 2028-01-01. The documents give neither the covenant definitions nor the company's ratios and state only that it was in compliance at 2026-06-30, so headroom is not established. For scale, on the unadjusted measure used here and with EBITDA flat, net debt would have to fall by USD 243.7 million to reach 3.75x, about 1.5 years of last-twelve-months free cash flow, which buybacks and acquisitions compete for. Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_embc.htm.jsonl, pages 52–53; 10-Q_2026-06-30_embc.htm.jsonl, page 21; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C1; calculation C2; calculation C5

Liquidity is adequate today but thinner than the headline and dated. Cash of USD 214.7 million and an undrawn revolver of USD 370.1 million gave USD 584.8 million at 2026-06-30, before letters of credit that are not stated. The 2026-08-06 amendment cut revolver commitments to USD 310.0 million; if the drawing of USD 129.9 million were unchanged, undrawn commitments would be USD 180.1 million and liquidity USD 394.8 million, USD 190.0 million lower. Commitments of USD 100.0 million still mature on 2027-03-31 and USD 139.4 million of debt falls due in fiscal 2027, which cash covers with USD 75.3 million to spare; how the drawing is split between the extended and non-extended commitments is not stated, and pro forma cash for the dividend is not established. Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_embc.htm.jsonl, pages 21–22; 10-Q_2026-06-30_embc.htm.jsonl, pages 52–53; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C6

Refinancing risk is back-ended, but ratings and market prices have already moved against the issuer. Of USD 1,469.3 million of principal, USD 1,318.0 million, 89.7%, falls due in fiscal 2029 and 2030: USD 618.0 million of term loan in March 2029 and USD 700.0 million of senior secured notes in February 2030. Moody's now rates the company B3 and S&P rates it B, both lower than the B1 and B+ reaffirmed in March 2026. The issuer's own estimate of the fair value of debt fell to 81.5% of carrying value at 2026-06-30 from 97.6% at 2026-03-31 while carrying value rose, and the extended revolver commitments cost 3.50% over SOFR against 3.00% for the part not extended, so lenders, holders and agencies are pricing more risk than the balance sheet shows. Agency reports, outlooks and rating triggers are not supplied, so the agencies' reasons and any trigger tied to the ratings are not established. Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_embc.htm.jsonl, pages 22, 42, 52; 10-Q_2026-03-31_embc.htm.jsonl, pages 18, 36; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C7; calculation C8; calculation C15

Financial policy has moved from deleveraging toward shareholder returns and acquisition, on a balance sheet with no equity cushion. Embecta prepaid USD 245.4 million of term loan voluntarily across fiscal 2025 and nine months 2026 and cut the quarterly dividend to USD 0.01 a share from USD 0.15, which saves USD 8.1 million a quarter. In the same nine months it paid USD 18.4 million of dividends, repurchased USD 8.7 million of shares under a USD 100.0 million authorisation and spent USD 128.4 million net on Owen Mumford, so free cash flow of USD 87.9 million did not cover the acquisition and total principal rose USD 52.5 million. Total equity is negative at USD -612.7 million, and the combined Chairman, President and Chief Executive role concentrates capital allocation authority. Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_embc.htm.jsonl, page 3; 10-Q_2026-06-30_embc.htm.jsonl, page 4; 10-Q_2026-06-30_embc.htm.jsonl, page 23; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C3; calculation C14

A single-source supply link to the former parent narrows strategic options, and diversification is still small. BD supplies all of Embecta's cannulas, owns the production and may end supply on a change of control, so a sale of the company is not a clean source of creditor protection; the annual value of purchases is not stated. Owen Mumford adds drug delivery devices from 2026-05-15 but contributed USD 13.8 million, 5.1% of third-quarter revenue, and its earnings are not stated, so diversification does not yet offset the United States decline. Basis: 10-K_2025-09-30_embc.htm.jsonl, page 5; 10-K_2025-09-30_embc.htm.jsonl, page 18; 10-Q_2026-06-30_embc.htm.jsonl, page 10; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C9

cells.text: Pen needles, syringes and safety devices for insulin injection; one operating segment with four product lines at the annual report date
Single product category: pricing or volume loss in pen needles flows straight to group cash flow
Pen needles were 68.6% of nine-month 2026 revenue and 72.6% of fiscal 2025 revenue; the United States was 46.0% of nine-month revenue after 53.6% in fiscal 2025
The profitable United States core is shrinking faster than international, which is the lower-priced base
Sales deductions for rebates, chargebacks, discounts and returns took 34.9% of gross sales in fiscal 2025 against 26.8% in fiscal 2023
Net price erosion is the first break in the model and it compounds volume loss
The three largest distributors, Cencora, McKesson and Cardinal Health, took about 42% of worldwide gross sales in fiscal 2025
A few buyers can press price or destock; individual shares are not stated
Novo Nordisk, MTD Group and Terumo Medical are named competitors; low-cost local providers and the shift from vials to pens have made the category highly competitive
Three manufacturing sites in Ireland, the United States and China; about 1,850 employees at 2025-09-30
Low capital need: capital expenditure was under 1% of revenue; footprint concentrates operating risk in three plants
BD sells all cannulas to Embecta under a supply agreement, owns the production and the related intellectual property, and may terminate on a change of control of Embecta
Single-source dependence on the former parent limits takeover and financing alternatives
Management attributes the second-quarter shortfall to increased competitive dynamics and softer overall market volumes in the United States
Management language, not independently verified; guidance assumes the dynamics continue

Owen Mumford adds drug delivery devices from 2026-05-15, and a generic GLP-1 co-packaging pipeline is building, with about 40% of identified partners in contract negotiations or having signed; Other revenue was 3.1% of nine-month 2026 revenue
Diversification is early and does not yet offset the United States decline

Over 75% of revenue is now carried by products launched and shipped under the embecta label; the transition is due to be substantially complete by the end of calendar 2026 and market-appropriate pen needles are under review by the United States FDA and BSI
Relabelling and registration add cost and regulatory delay risk but protect the brand once complete

runs.text: The credit rests on four supports. Cash conversion is the strongest: free cash flow of USD 164.6 million is 61.9% of reported EBITDA with capital expenditure at 0.9% of revenue, so scheduled term loan amortisation of USD 9.5 million a year is covered 17.33 times by free cash flow after interest. The maturity runway is the second: apart from small scheduled amortisation and the revolver, no principal falls due before March 2029, and the senior secured notes of USD 700.0 million carry fixed rates, 47.6% of principal. Third, management has shown it will favour lenders when pressed, with USD 245.4 million of voluntary prepayments and a dividend cut. Fourth, international revenue rose 7.5% and the generic GLP-1 co-packaging pipeline gives a route to growth outside United States pen needles. Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_embc.htm.jsonl, page 4; 10-Q_2026-06-30_embc.htm.jsonl, page 22; EX99.1_2026-06-30_embc_q32026ex-991-htm.htm.jsonl, page 2; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C2; calculation C3; calculation C7

The credit has five weaknesses. The first and most important is price and volume erosion in United States pen needles, with gross margin at 58.7% against 63.5%. Second, net leverage of 4.67x, unchanged at 4.67x on pro forma net debt of USD 1,241.0 million for the dividend payable on 2026-09-15, is rising into tighter covenants. Third, revenue is concentrated: pen needles were 68.6% of nine-month revenue, the United States 46.0% and three distributors about 42% of gross sales. Fourth, 89.7% of principal is due in fiscal 2029 and 2030, both agencies cut their ratings in May 2026 and the debt is marked at 81.5% of carrying value. Fifth, financial policy and structure add risk: buybacks and a debt-funded acquisition at rising leverage, negative total equity and a single-source supplier that can end supply on a change of control. Basis: EX99.1_2026-06-30_embc_q32026ex-991-htm.htm.jsonl, pages 2–4; 10-K_2025-09-30_embc.htm.jsonl, page 26; 10-Q_2026-06-30_embc.htm.jsonl, pages 22, 42; Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C1; calculation C7; calculation C8; calculation C9; calculation C10; calculation C15

blocks.title: Transaction summary and new debt issues

runs.text: The only completed transaction in the period is the acquisition of Owen Mumford, a UK medical device and drug delivery company founded in 1952, which closed on 2026-05-15. The upfront cash payment was GBP 126.0 million (USD 169.9 million) including estimated acquired cash, with up to GBP 50.0 million more payable on sales of its auto-injector platform; purchase consideration was USD 208.0 million including contingent consideration of USD 38.1 million at fair value, and the final price is subject to a working capital adjustment. Basis: EX99.1_2026-03-31_embc_ss6329586-ex9901-htm.htm.jsonl, pages 1–2; 10-Q_2026-06-30_embc.htm.jsonl, pages 8–9; 10-Q_2026-06-30_embc.htm.jsonl, page 34

Embecta funded the closing by drawing about USD 180.0 million on its revolver and had repaid USD 50.1 million by 2026-06-30, leaving USD 129.9 million drawn. No new bonds or term debt were issued in fiscal 2026; the notes and the term loan date from the 2022 separation financing and are unchanged apart from term loan prepayments. Basis: EX99.1_2026-06-30_embc_q32026ex-991-htm.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-Q_2026-06-30_embc.htm.jsonl, page 22; 10-K_2025-09-30_embc.htm.jsonl, page 128

After the period, on 2026-08-06, the first lien credit agreement was amended: revolver commitments fell from USD 500.0 million to USD 310.0 million, USD 210.0 million of them were extended to 2028-12-30 at SOFR plus 3.50% and USD 100.0 million still matures on 2027-03-31, and covenants and monthly liquidity reporting for revolving lenders were added. This is a subsequent event and is not folded into any period figure. Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_embc.htm.jsonl, pages 52–53

Capital allocation actions around the deal were a three-year USD 100.0 million buyback authorisation, with USD 8.7 million repurchased, a cut in the quarterly dividend from USD 0.15 to USD 0.01 a share and the sale of patch pump intellectual property and assets for USD 10.0 million. Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_embc.htm.jsonl, page 23; 10-Q_2026-06-30_embc.htm.jsonl, page 34; 10-K_2025-09-30_embc.htm.jsonl, page 141

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Financial foundation for Embecta Corp. (issuer id embc-1872789), as of 2026-11-18, on the credit snapshot pathway. Scope: normalised statements, debt, net debt, leverage, cover and liquidity inputs for fiscal 2023 to 2025 and the nine months to 2026-06-30, from the nine supplied filings and releases.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Embecta's net leverage rose to 4.67x last-twelve-months EBITDA at 2026-06-30 from 4.12x at the 2025 year end, as revolver-funded acquisition spending met falling United States revenue, leaving creditors a thinner cushion.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Net debt rose USD 67.7 million to USD 1,240.4 million while reported EBITDA for the last twelve months fell to USD 265.8 million from USD 284.3 million. Pro forma for the dividend payable on 2026-09-15, net debt is approximately USD 1,241.0 million.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_embc.htm.jsonl, pages 2–5; 10-Q_2026-06-30_embc.htm.jsonl, page 22; calculation C2; calculation C5; calculation C8; calculation C14; calculation C15

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Cash interest cover was 2.74x at the 2025 year end and is not calculable for the latest twelve months. Cash of USD 214.7 million and an undrawn revolver of USD 370.1 million at 2026-06-30 are tempered by a revolver cut to USD 310.0 million on 2026-08-06 and USD 139.4 million of debt due in fiscal 2027. Issuer-adjusted EBITDA cannot be built for any twelve-month period, so every ratio uses the unadjusted measure.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_embc.htm.jsonl, pages 21–22; 10-Q_2026-06-30_embc.htm.jsonl, pages 52–53; calculation C9; calculation C12

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Leverage improved through fiscal 2025 and then reversed. Net debt over reported EBITDA fell from 6.78x at the 2024 year end to 4.12x at the 2025 year end, helped by USD 184.6 million of term loan repayments and by a fall in other operating expense, net from USD 124.5 million to USD 65.4 million that lifted fiscal 2025 EBITDA to USD 284.3 million from USD 192.7 million. The fiscal 2024 base was depressed by separation and restructuring costs, so part of the improvement is a lower cost base, not a stronger business. Since September 2025 the ratio has risen to 4.67x as USD 180.0 million was drawn on the revolver for the Owen Mumford acquisition, USD 128.4 million of cash left for the purchase net of cash acquired, and EBITDA fell.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-09-30_embc.htm.jsonl, pages 101–103; 10-Q_2026-06-30_embc.htm.jsonl, pages 2–5; calculation C4; calculation C8; calculation C15

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The earnings trend is weaker than reported EBITDA suggests. Nine-month revenue fell 7.6% to USD 754.7 million. United States revenue fell 20.6% and pen needles, the largest product family, fell 13.2%, while Owen Mumford added USD 13.8 million after its 2026-05-15 closing. Reported EBITDA fell only 8.6% to USD 197.6 million because the prior-year nine months carried USD 45.4 million of patch pump costs that the issuer adds back, whereas issuer-adjusted EBITDA fell 23.9% to USD 247.5 million. Leverage on reported EBITDA therefore likely understates the pressure creditors face on the operating run rate; the adjusted ratio cannot be built because fiscal 2025 adjusted EBITDA is not stated.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: EX99.1_2026-06-30_embc_q32026ex-991-htm.htm.jsonl, pages 2–4; EX99.1_2026-06-30_embc_q32026ex-991-htm.htm.jsonl, pages 8–11; calculation C13; calculation C18

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Free cash flow stayed positive but was supported by receivable sales. Free cash flow was USD 87.9 million in nine months 2026 against USD 105.7 million a year earlier, and USD 167.2 million of trade receivables, 22.2% of nine-month revenue, were sold to a third-party buyer on an uncommitted basis and moved cash into operating activities. If the buyer withdrew, working capital would absorb cash equal to the receivables then held by the buyer, an amount the filings do not state.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_embc.htm.jsonl, page 4; 10-Q_2026-06-30_embc.htm.jsonl, page 25; calculation C16; calculation C20

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Interest cover is modest. Reported EBITDA covered cash interest 2.74x in fiscal 2025 after 1.64x in fiscal 2024 and 2.21x in fiscal 2023, and the last twelve months cannot be calculated because cash interest for nine months 2025 is not stated. Nine-month interest expense, net fell to USD 70.6 million from USD 81.2 million as debt was repaid, so cover is unlikely to have worsened sharply, although quarterly interest expense, net edged up to USD 23.9 million in the third quarter from USD 22.6 million in the second as the revolver was drawn.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-09-30_embc.htm.jsonl, page 113; 10-Q_2026-06-30_embc.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-Q_2026-03-31_embc.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-Q_2026-06-30_embc.htm.jsonl, page 22; calculation C9; calculation C21

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Liquidity is adequate on the face of the balance sheet but the dated structure matters. Cash was USD 214.7 million and the undrawn revolver USD 370.1 million before any letters of credit, which are not stated. The 2026-08-06 amendment cut commitments to USD 310.0 million, keeps USD 100.0 million maturing in March 2027 and extends USD 210.0 million to December 2028 at a higher margin. Debt maturing is USD 139.4 million in fiscal 2027, USD 618.0 million in fiscal 2029 and USD 700.0 million in fiscal 2030, and the estimated fair value of debt fell to 81.5% of carrying value at 2026-06-30 from 97.6% at 2026-03-31, a market signal that Market-implied risk should weigh.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_embc.htm.jsonl, pages 21–22; 10-Q_2026-06-30_embc.htm.jsonl, pages 52–53; 10-Q_2026-03-31_embc.htm.jsonl, page 18; calculation C12; calculation C17

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest contrary evidence is cash flow: nine-month free cash flow stayed positive at USD 87.9 million, USD 70.3 million of term loan prepayments were voluntary, interest expense, net is falling and guidance for adjusted operating margin was raised in August. The view would improve if fiscal 2026 results show twelve-month reported EBITDA recovering above the fiscal 2025 level of USD 284.3 million with the revolver repaid, and it would worsen if United States revenue keeps falling at the nine-month pace or the receivable buyer limits purchases.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Business & governance for Embecta Corp. (issuer id embc-1872789), as of 2026-11-18, on the credit snapshot pathway. Scope: business and operating model, ownership and control, former-parent dependence, governance, financial policy and transactions, from the nine supplied filings and releases.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Embecta is a listed diabetes injection supplier with no identified sponsor whose core United States pen needle business is eroding on price and volume, so creditors depend on a shrinking cash engine and a former parent that supplies its key input.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-09-30_embc.htm.jsonl, page 4; 10-K_2025-09-30_embc.htm.jsonl, page 5; 10-K_2025-09-30_embc.htm.jsonl, page 77; calculation C2

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: United States revenue fell 20.6% in nine months 2026 and the share of gross sales lost to rebates and discounts rose from 26.8% in fiscal 2023 to 34.9% in fiscal 2025. In May 2026 management cut the quarterly dividend to USD 0.01 a share and authorised a USD 100.0 million buyback, and it closed a revolver-funded acquisition, which moves financial policy from deleveraging toward shareholder returns and growth. Ownership and board detail are only partly documented, so governance risk is rated Medium.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: EX99.1_2026-06-30_embc_q32026ex-991-htm.htm.jsonl, pages 3–4; 10-K_2025-09-30_embc.htm.jsonl, page 122; 10-Q_2026-06-30_embc.htm.jsonl, pages 23, 34; calculation C2; calculation C3

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The core is concentrated and commoditising, and the damage is in the United States. Pen needles were 68.6% of nine-month revenue, United States revenue fell 20.6% and pen needles fell 13.2%, with volume costing USD 60.0 million and price USD 27.4 million of revenue. Rebates and discounts took 34.9% of gross sales in fiscal 2025 against 26.8% two years earlier, so competition is already reaching net price, and gross margin fell to 58.7% from 63.5%. Management blames increased competitive dynamics and soft market volumes and assumes they persist, which means the decline in earnings per unit of debt is not a one-quarter event.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: EX99.1_2026-06-30_embc_q32026ex-991-htm.htm.jsonl, pages 2–4; 10-K_2025-09-30_embc.htm.jsonl, page 122; EX99.1_2026-03-31_embc_q22026ex-991-htm.htm.jsonl, page 2; calculation C1; calculation C2; calculation C3; calculation C11

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Dependence on the former parent is structural and narrows strategic options. BD sells Embecta all of its cannulas, keeps the production and the intellectual property, leases the Holdrege plant to Embecta and may end cannula supply if Embecta changes control, while a tax agreement bars certain actions without a BD opinion or consent. A takeover, large equity issue or sale of the company is therefore not a clean source of creditor protection, and supply risk sits with a counterparty that cannot be replaced quickly; the annual purchase value from BD is not stated.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Financial policy was creditor-friendly in fiscal 2025 and has turned mixed in 2026. Embecta prepaid USD 175.1 million of term loan voluntarily in fiscal 2025 and USD 70.3 million in nine months 2026, and cut the quarterly dividend, which saves USD 8.1 million a quarter. In the same nine months it repaid USD 127.5 million of debt, drew USD 180.0 million on the revolver for the acquisition, so total principal rose by USD 52.5 million, and it began a USD 100.0 million buyback although management had said it expected to repay about USD 150 million of debt during 2026. Cash that could repay revolver debt is being split with equity holders while leverage is rising.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-09-30_embc.htm.jsonl, page 129; 10-Q_2026-06-30_embc.htm.jsonl, pages 22–23; EX99.1_2026-03-31_embc_q22026ex-991-htm.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-Q_2026-06-30_embc.htm.jsonl, page 34; calculation C5; calculation C6; calculation C12

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The Owen Mumford acquisition diversifies the business but adds debt, an earn-out and integration risk before it adds earnings. Purchase consideration was USD 208.0 million, including contingent consideration with a fair value of USD 38.9 million at 2026-06-30 and a maximum of GBP 50.0 million, and the target contributed USD 13.8 million, 5.1% of third-quarter revenue, after closing. Other revenue was only 3.1% of nine-month revenue, so diversification does not yet offset the United States decline, and the 2026 integration and acquisition costs reduce free cash flow.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_embc.htm.jsonl, pages 8–10; 10-Q_2026-06-30_embc.htm.jsonl, page 28; 10-Q_2026-06-30_embc.htm.jsonl, page 34; calculation C7; calculation C10

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Reporting control has improved but event risk has risen. A material weakness in internal control first reported for fiscal 2024 was concluded remediated at 2025-09-30, which supports confidence in reported figures, yet a securities class action over fiscal 2026 revenue guidance was filed on 2026-06-17 and the filing says no loss range can be estimated. The combined Chairman, President and Chief Executive Officer role concentrates authority over capital allocation, and an independent lead director is not stated.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Ownership is the largest information gap. No sponsor or controlling holder is identified and only a few thousand holders of record are stated, which removes sponsor extraction risk and sponsor support alike; creditors rely on internal cash flow and board policy. Beneficial ownership, the remaining stake of the former parent and board consent rights are in a proxy statement that was not supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest contrary evidence is that international revenue grew 7.5% in nine months 2026 to 54.0% of revenue, over 75% of revenue is already carried by products relaunched under the embecta label, about 40% of identified GLP-1 co-packaging partners are in negotiations or have signed, and management raised its adjusted margin and earnings guidance in August while reaffirming revenue guidance. Voluntary prepayments of USD 245.4 million over fiscal 2025 and nine months 2026 and the dividend cut show a willingness to favour lenders when pressed. The view would improve if United States revenue stabilised for two consecutive quarters, if regulators cleared the market-appropriate pen needles, or if the executed documents showed no change-of-control hazard, and it would worsen if buybacks accelerate or cannula supply is disrupted.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: EX99.1_2026-06-30_embc_q32026ex-991-htm.htm.jsonl, pages 2–4; EX99.1_2026-03-31_embc_q22026ex-991-htm.htm.jsonl, page 4; calculation C2; calculation C12

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Beneficial ownership, board composition and consent rights sit in a proxy statement that was not supplied, so the finding that no sponsor or controlling holder exists rests on silence in the annual report and would change if a large holder were named.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The executed credit agreement, indentures and former-parent agreements were not supplied, so the finding on cannula supply and change-of-control exposure rests on the annual report summary and the capacity of the company to fund buybacks cannot be assessed.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - No document after 2026-08-07 is supplied, so the view that financial policy has turned toward buybacks could change if the cost review, a faster buyback pace or the fiscal 2026 annual results have since been published.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The only completed transaction in the period is the acquisition of Owen Mumford, a UK medical device and drug delivery company founded in 1952, which closed on 2026-05-15. The upfront cash payment was GBP 126.0 million (USD 169.9 million) including estimated acquired cash, with up to GBP 50.0 million more payable on sales of its auto-injector platform; purchase consideration was USD 208.0 million including contingent consideration of USD 38.1 million at fair value, and the final price is subject to a working capital adjustment.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Embecta funded the closing by drawing about USD 180.0 million on its revolver and had repaid USD 50.1 million by 2026-06-30, leaving USD 129.9 million drawn. No new bonds or term debt were issued in fiscal 2026; the notes and the term loan date from the 2022 separation financing and are unchanged apart from term loan prepayments.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: After the period, on 2026-08-06, the first lien credit agreement was amended: revolver commitments fell from USD 500.0 million to USD 310.0 million, USD 210.0 million of them were extended to 2028-12-30 at SOFR plus 3.50% and USD 100.0 million still matures on 2027-03-31, and covenants and monthly liquidity reporting for revolving lenders were added. This is a subsequent event and is not folded into any period figure.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Capital allocation actions around the deal were a three-year USD 100.0 million buyback authorisation, with USD 8.7 million repurchased, a cut in the quarterly dividend from USD 0.15 to USD 0.01 a share and the sale of patch pump intellectual property and assets for USD 10.0 million.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Sponsor / Governance Risk Level: Medium. The risk level is driven by buybacks and a debt-funded acquisition at rising leverage, because cash and debt capacity move toward equity and growth while the core earns less, which implies a weaker deleveraging path for creditors. Countervailing evidence is the dividend cut, the voluntary term loan prepayments and the remediated control weakness.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Fundamental credit for Embecta Corp. (issuer id embc-1872789), as of 2026-11-18, on the credit snapshot pathway. Scope: the overall credit profile, strongest support, weakest dimension and primary downside path, from the nine supplied filings and releases and the accepted analyses of Source readiness, Financial foundation and Business & governance.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Embecta is a weak and weakening credit: cash generation is still sound, but United States pen needle earnings are eroding, leverage is rising and cash is going to equity holders, leaving creditors little cushion if the decline continues.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C1; calculation C9

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Net leverage rose to 4.67x at 2026-06-30 from 4.12x at the 2025 year end, and pro forma for the dividend payable on 2026-09-15 net debt is USD 1,241.0 million and net leverage 4.67x. Both agencies cut their ratings in May 2026, to B3 from B1 at Moody's and to B from B+ at S&P. Free cash flow of USD 164.6 million over the last twelve months is the main support, but it was far lower in earlier years and the revolver covenants tighten from 2028. Headroom against them is not established because the definitions are not supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-06-30_embc.htm.jsonl, pages 52–53; 10-Q_2026-06-30_embc.htm.jsonl, page 42; 10-Q_2026-03-31_embc.htm.jsonl, page 36; calculation C1; calculation C2; calculation C5; calculation C15

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The core business is losing price and volume in the United States, and that is where the earnings come from. United States revenue fell 20.6% in nine months 2026 and pen needle revenue fell 13.2%, while group revenue lost USD 60.0 million to volume and USD 27.4 million to price against nine-month revenue of USD 816.4 million a year earlier. Cost of products sold rose to USD 311.9 million from USD 298.1 million while revenue fell, so price concessions went straight to gross profit and gross margin dropped to 58.7% from 63.5%. Management attributes the shortfall to competition and soft market volumes and assumes both continue for the rest of the year, so the erosion should be read as the base case, not a one-quarter event.

fields.value: Basis: EX99.1_2026-06-30_embc_q32026ex-991-htm.htm.jsonl, pages 2–4; 10-Q_2026-06-30_embc.htm.jsonl, page 34; EX99.1_2026-03-31_embc_q22026ex-991-htm.htm.jsonl, page 2; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C9; calculation C10

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Management's raised margin guidance still implies a weaker fourth quarter than the third. Fiscal 2026 revenue guidance of USD 1,015 million to USD 1,035 million implies fourth-quarter revenue of USD 260.3 million to USD 280.3 million against USD 271.7 million in the third quarter, and adjusted operating margin guidance of 23.50% to 24.00%, with adjusted revenue equal to reported revenue as in every reported period, implies fourth-quarter adjusted operating income of USD 41.2 million to USD 51.1 million against USD 69.4 million in the third quarter. The documents do not explain the step-down, which is either caution or a heavier fourth quarter, so the third-quarter run rate should not be annualised.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Cash flow is the main support, but it has been volatile and is partly funded by receivable sales. Free cash flow of USD 164.6 million over the last twelve months is 61.9% of reported EBITDA and capital expenditure is only 0.9% of revenue, so there is a real source of debt service. The record is less steady: free cash flow was USD 41.2 million, USD 19.9 million and USD 182.4 million in fiscal 2023, 2024 and 2025, and nine-month free cash flow fell to USD 87.9 million from USD 105.7 million. In nine months 2026 USD 167.2 million of trade receivables, 22.2% of revenue, were sold to a third party on an uncommitted basis, 2.6 times the USD 63.2 million sold in all of fiscal 2025, so part of operating cash flow depends on a buyer that can stop purchasing; the outstanding sold balance is not established.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-09-30_embc.htm.jsonl, pages 103, 135; 10-Q_2026-06-30_embc.htm.jsonl, page 4; 10-Q_2026-06-30_embc.htm.jsonl, page 25; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C2; calculation C3

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Leverage has turned up while the covenant path asks for the opposite. Net debt rose USD 67.7 million to USD 1,240.4 million between 2025-09-30 and 2026-06-30 while last-twelve-months reported EBITDA fell to USD 265.8 million from USD 284.3 million, taking net leverage to 4.67x from 4.12x; pro forma for the dividend payable on 2026-09-15 the figures are USD 1,241.0 million and 4.67x. The amended revolver tests a first lien net leverage ratio of at most 4.75x through 2027-06-30 that steps down to 3.75x from 2028-04-01, and an interest coverage ratio of at least 2.50x that steps up to 3.00x from 2028-01-01. The documents give neither the covenant definitions nor the company's ratios and state only that it was in compliance at 2026-06-30, so headroom is not established. For scale, on the unadjusted measure used here and with EBITDA flat, net debt would have to fall by USD 243.7 million to reach 3.75x, about 1.5 years of last-twelve-months free cash flow, which buybacks and acquisitions compete for.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_embc.htm.jsonl, pages 52–53; 10-Q_2026-06-30_embc.htm.jsonl, page 21; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C1; calculation C2; calculation C5

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Liquidity is adequate today but thinner than the headline and dated. Cash of USD 214.7 million and an undrawn revolver of USD 370.1 million gave USD 584.8 million at 2026-06-30, before letters of credit that are not stated. The 2026-08-06 amendment cut revolver commitments to USD 310.0 million; if the drawing of USD 129.9 million were unchanged, undrawn commitments would be USD 180.1 million and liquidity USD 394.8 million, USD 190.0 million lower. Commitments of USD 100.0 million still mature on 2027-03-31 and USD 139.4 million of debt falls due in fiscal 2027, which cash covers with USD 75.3 million to spare; how the drawing is split between the extended and non-extended commitments is not stated, and pro forma cash for the dividend is not established.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_embc.htm.jsonl, pages 21–22; 10-Q_2026-06-30_embc.htm.jsonl, pages 52–53; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C6

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Refinancing risk is back-ended, but ratings and market prices have already moved against the issuer. Of USD 1,469.3 million of principal, USD 1,318.0 million, 89.7%, falls due in fiscal 2029 and 2030: USD 618.0 million of term loan in March 2029 and USD 700.0 million of senior secured notes in February 2030. Moody's now rates the company B3 and S&P rates it B, both lower than the B1 and B+ reaffirmed in March 2026. The issuer's own estimate of the fair value of debt fell to 81.5% of carrying value at 2026-06-30 from 97.6% at 2026-03-31 while carrying value rose, and the extended revolver commitments cost 3.50% over SOFR against 3.00% for the part not extended, so lenders, holders and agencies are pricing more risk than the balance sheet shows. Agency reports, outlooks and rating triggers are not supplied, so the agencies' reasons and any trigger tied to the ratings are not established.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_embc.htm.jsonl, pages 22, 42, 52; 10-Q_2026-03-31_embc.htm.jsonl, pages 18, 36; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C7; calculation C8; calculation C15

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Financial policy has moved from deleveraging toward shareholder returns and acquisition, on a balance sheet with no equity cushion. Embecta prepaid USD 245.4 million of term loan voluntarily across fiscal 2025 and nine months 2026 and cut the quarterly dividend to USD 0.01 a share from USD 0.15, which saves USD 8.1 million a quarter. In the same nine months it paid USD 18.4 million of dividends, repurchased USD 8.7 million of shares under a USD 100.0 million authorisation and spent USD 128.4 million net on Owen Mumford, so free cash flow of USD 87.9 million did not cover the acquisition and total principal rose USD 52.5 million. Total equity is negative at USD -612.7 million, and the combined Chairman, President and Chief Executive role concentrates capital allocation authority.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_embc.htm.jsonl, page 3; 10-Q_2026-06-30_embc.htm.jsonl, page 4; 10-Q_2026-06-30_embc.htm.jsonl, page 23; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C3; calculation C14

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: A single-source supply link to the former parent narrows strategic options, and diversification is still small. BD supplies all of Embecta's cannulas, owns the production and may end supply on a change of control, so a sale of the company is not a clean source of creditor protection; the annual value of purchases is not stated. Owen Mumford adds drug delivery devices from 2026-05-15 but contributed USD 13.8 million, 5.1% of third-quarter revenue, and its earnings are not stated, so diversification does not yet offset the United States decline.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-09-30_embc.htm.jsonl, page 5; 10-K_2025-09-30_embc.htm.jsonl, page 18; 10-Q_2026-06-30_embc.htm.jsonl, page 10; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C9

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest contrary evidence is momentum and cash. Third-quarter revenue rose USD 49.9 million from the second quarter to USD 271.7 million, of which USD 13.8 million was Owen Mumford, and the United States decline eased to 24.6% from 29.4%. Management raised its fiscal 2026 adjusted operating margin range to 23.50% to 24.00% from 22.25% to 23.25%, interest expense, net fell to USD 70.6 million from USD 81.2 million in nine months, and USD 245.4 million of voluntary term loan prepayments show a willingness to favour lenders. Management states that cash, operating cash flow and revolver capacity are sufficient for the foreseeable future and that its credit profile should give access to financing to meet upcoming maturities, a statement the May 2026 rating cuts and the fair value of the debt qualify.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: EX99.1_2026-06-30_embc_q32026ex-991-htm.htm.jsonl, pages 1–5; EX99.1_2026-03-31_embc_q22026ex-991-htm.htm.jsonl, page 3; 10-Q_2026-06-30_embc.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-Q_2026-06-30_embc.htm.jsonl, page 39; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C9; calculation C4; calculation C3; calculation C15

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The view would improve if United States revenue stabilised for two consecutive quarters, if net leverage returned below 4.12x with the revolver repaid, if the USD 100.0 million of commitments due on 2027-03-31 were extended, or if the executed covenant definitions showed ample headroom. It would worsen if the United States decline widened beyond the second-quarter rate, if buybacks accelerated while the revolver is drawn, or if the receivable buyer limited purchases.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_embc.htm.jsonl, pages 52–53; EX99.1_2026-03-31_embc_q22026ex-991-htm.htm.jsonl, page 3; calculation C1; calculation C3; calculation C6

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Covenant definitions, covenant EBITDA and the company's covenant ratios are not supplied, so the statements that the covenant path tightens carry levels only and the conclusion on deleveraging pressure carries no headroom estimate.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - No document reports the fiscal year that ended on 2026-09-30, so the leverage, liquidity and guidance conclusions describe 2026-06-30 and could be overtaken by fourth-quarter results or by whether the dividend payable on 2026-09-15 was paid.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Letters of credit and the split of the revolver drawing between the extended and non-extended commitments are not stated, so liquidity of USD 584.8 million may be overstated and the amount to be refinanced by 2027-03-31 is not established.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The fair value of debt is one issuer estimate at one date, not a traded price, so the conclusion that the market is marking the debt down cannot be tied to any single instrument.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The credit rests on four supports. Cash conversion is the strongest: free cash flow of USD 164.6 million is 61.9% of reported EBITDA with capital expenditure at 0.9% of revenue, so scheduled term loan amortisation of USD 9.5 million a year is covered 17.33 times by free cash flow after interest. The maturity runway is the second: apart from small scheduled amortisation and the revolver, no principal falls due before March 2029, and the senior secured notes of USD 700.0 million carry fixed rates, 47.6% of principal. Third, management has shown it will favour lenders when pressed, with USD 245.4 million of voluntary prepayments and a dividend cut. Fourth, international revenue rose 7.5% and the generic GLP-1 co-packaging pipeline gives a route to growth outside United States pen needles.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_embc.htm.jsonl, page 4; 10-Q_2026-06-30_embc.htm.jsonl, page 22; EX99.1_2026-06-30_embc_q32026ex-991-htm.htm.jsonl, page 2; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C2; calculation C3; calculation C7

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The credit has five weaknesses. The first and most important is price and volume erosion in United States pen needles, with gross margin at 58.7% against 63.5%. Second, net leverage of 4.67x, unchanged at 4.67x on pro forma net debt of USD 1,241.0 million for the dividend payable on 2026-09-15, is rising into tighter covenants. Third, revenue is concentrated: pen needles were 68.6% of nine-month revenue, the United States 46.0% and three distributors about 42% of gross sales. Fourth, 89.7% of principal is due in fiscal 2029 and 2030, both agencies cut their ratings in May 2026 and the debt is marked at 81.5% of carrying value. Fifth, financial policy and structure add risk: buybacks and a debt-funded acquisition at rising leverage, negative total equity and a single-source supplier that can end supply on a change of control.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: EX99.1_2026-06-30_embc_q32026ex-991-htm.htm.jsonl, pages 2–4; 10-K_2025-09-30_embc.htm.jsonl, page 26; 10-Q_2026-06-30_embc.htm.jsonl, pages 22, 42; Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C1; calculation C7; calculation C8; calculation C9; calculation C10; calculation C15

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Module status: Ready with Limitations. The nine supplied filings and releases cover fiscal 2023 to the quarter ended 2026-06-30, and the accepted analyses supply the statements, net debt, leverage and business facts used here. The latest document is dated 2026-08-07, 103 days before the as-of date, and no document covers the fiscal year that ended 2026-09-30. Agency reports and rating outlooks, peer data, executed legal documents, covenant certificates and a proxy statement are not supplied, so conclusions on covenants, relative standing and ownership are bounded accordingly. Source readiness lists ratings among the blank run inputs and does not map ratings work; the issuer does state its current ratings in the latest quarterly report, which this analysis uses, so that limit applies only to agency reports, outlooks and triggers.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Source readiness (CP-0); 10-Q_2026-06-30_embc.htm.jsonl, pages 42, 54; calculation C14; calculation C15

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The datapoints taken from earlier analyses are used as stated: net debt of USD 1,240.4 million at 2026-06-30, which is USD 1,241.0 million pro forma for the dividend payable on 2026-09-15, last-twelve-months reported EBITDA of USD 265.8 million, net leverage of 4.67x (4.67x pro forma), free cash flow of USD 164.6 million and principal of USD 1,469.3 million. No earlier analysis has a period or entity mismatch with this run, and the measure differences that remain are logged under Gaps.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Source readiness (CP-0); calculation C1; calculation C2

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Embecta sells pen needles, syringes and safety devices for insulin injection from three manufacturing sites, in one operating segment. Pen needles were 68.6% of nine-month 2026 revenue and the United States 46.0%, down from 53.6% in fiscal 2025. Demand follows insulin users and recurs, which supports cash flow visibility, but the business is concentrated in pen needles, with three distributors taking about 42% of gross sales in fiscal 2025, so a price or volume loss in United States pen needles reaches group cash flow directly and lenders have no second earnings engine yet. Owen Mumford, acquired on 2026-05-15, adds drug delivery devices but is small.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-09-30_embc.htm.jsonl, page 5; 10-K_2025-09-30_embc.htm.jsonl, page 26; EX99.1_2026-06-30_embc_q32026ex-991-htm.htm.jsonl, pages 3–4; calculation C9

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Embecta is a listed company with no identified sponsor or controlling holder and a few thousand holders of record, which removes sponsor extraction risk and also sponsor support, so creditors rely on internal cash flow and board policy. BD, the former parent, supplies all cannulas, leases the Holdrege plant and can end supply on a change of control, so a sale of the company cannot be assumed to benefit creditors. Beneficial ownership and board consent rights sit in a proxy statement that was not supplied, and the guarantor group is described only generically, so structural subordination of any creditor class is not assessed here.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Revenue is recurring and non-discretionary for insulin users, regulated and reimbursed by payers, concentrated in pen needles and the United States, exposed to substitution and structurally declining in the United States. Sales deductions took 34.9% of gross sales in fiscal 2025 against 26.8% in fiscal 2023, and in nine months 2026 price cost USD 27.4 million, 3.4% of prior-year revenue, and volume USD 60.0 million, 7.3%. Low-cost local providers, the shift from vials to pens, new entrants offering payers more choice and proposed competitive bidding for diabetes devices all act on price, so pricing power is weak and the first break in the credit is net price, which volume loss then compounds.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-09-30_embc.htm.jsonl, page 122; 10-K_2025-09-30_embc.htm.jsonl, pages 23, 80; EX99.1_2026-06-30_embc_q32026ex-991-htm.htm.jsonl, page 4; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C9

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: International revenue rose 7.5% in nine months 2026, only 3.6% at adjusted constant currency, and does not offset the United States fall of 20.6%. Contract duration, renewal rates and churn are not stated, so revenue visibility beyond the next quarter rests on management's assumption that the second-quarter dynamics persist.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Margins are being defended by cost relief that will not repeat, so resilience is weak. Gross profit fell USD 75.5 million in nine months 2026 on a revenue fall of USD 61.7 million because cost of products sold rose, and the USD 27.4 million price effect alone is 36.3% of the gross profit decline; gross margin fell 4.8 percentage points to 58.7%. Operating income fell only 10.0% because operating expenses fell USD 56.9 million to USD 275.8 million, helped by the discontinued patch pump program, which carried USD 45.4 million of costs in the prior-year nine months, and a USD 10.1 million gain on the sale of its assets.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_embc.htm.jsonl, pages 4, 34; EX99.1_2026-06-30_embc_q32026ex-991-htm.htm.jsonl, pages 2–4; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C10

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Reported EBITDA margin held at 26.1% over the last twelve months against 26.3% in fiscal 2025, but issuer-adjusted EBITDA fell 23.9% in nine months 2026 to USD 247.5 million from USD 325.4 million. A cost review began in May 2026 and its outcome is not stated, so there is no evidence yet of cost flexibility large enough to defend margins under further United States volume loss.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-06-30_embc.htm.jsonl, page 34; calculation C10

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Capital intensity is low, which gives cash flexibility, but it is low partly because investment has fallen. Capital expenditure was USD 9.3 million in fiscal 2025, 22.9% of depreciation and amortisation of USD 40.7 million, and USD 2.2 million in nine months 2026, 7.1% of USD 31.1 million, while research and development expense fell 52.3% to USD 15.6 million from USD 32.7 million. The split between maintenance and growth capital is not stated, so the room to cut further cannot be sized.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Free cash flow conversion of 61.9% of reported EBITDA is after cash interest and working capital, and it covers scheduled amortisation 17.33 times. At that rate repaying net debt would take 7.5 years, so deleveraging depends on EBITDA stabilising and on cash being kept for debt, not on a single strong year; acquisition and integration costs and the receivable sales discussed above add variability.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-06-30_embc.htm.jsonl, page 4; calculation C2

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Rivalry is intense and takes the form of price. Novo Nordisk, MTD Group and Terumo Medical compete in diabetes injection, local low-cost providers have entered, and the shift from vials to pens has made the category highly competitive, so sales deductions rise and net price erodes; creditors face lower gross profit per unit and less pricing room to defend EBITDA.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Entry is easier than the brand suggests. Competitors new to pen needles and syringes have started to engage payers and give them more formulary choice, while Embecta's own market-appropriate pen needles are still under review by the United States FDA and BSI, so its lower-cost response is not yet available and pricing pressure continues in the meantime.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Substitutes act on volume. Oral and once-weekly therapies, including GLP-1s and once-weekly insulin, have delayed insulin initiation and reduced demand, and insulin therapy in developed markets continues to move to infusion pumps. The same GLP-1 trend gives a co-packaging opening, with launches in India, Canada and Brazil and a United States small pack expected, but that revenue is not quantified, so it cannot yet offset lost pen needle volume.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Buyer power sits with three distributors that took about 42% of gross sales and with payers that control formulary access; proposed competitive bidding by the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services would add a price-setting buyer. Buyer power is the direct route from payer decisions to the sales deductions that reached 34.9% of gross sales.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Supplier power is the force that can stop sales outright. BD is the sole source of cannulas and may end supply on a change of control, some resins and rubber stoppers are not always available from multiple sources, and tariffs may raise the cost of goods, so a supply interruption would stop sales while fixed costs and debt service continue.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: These factors are material to the credit, so they are assessed. Tariffs and local-sourcing preferences may raise input costs and let local competitors price aggressively; proposed price negotiation and competitive bidding by United States payers could cut net price further; and the Italian payback measure remains a source of revenue estimates. A weaker United States dollar added USD 14.8 million to nine-month revenue, so reported revenue benefits from currency and would lose that help if the dollar strengthened.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Rates matter because 52.4% of principal floats: the issuer states that a change of 100 bp in interest rates would move annual interest expense by USD 7.7 million, and no interest rate hedge is described, since the derivative disclosures list only currency forward contracts. Social and technological shifts, an ageing population, care moving outside hospitals, weekly drug therapies and pumps, change who uses pen needles and how often, and the effect on volume is not quantified in the documents.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_embc.htm.jsonl, page 50; 10-K_2025-09-30_embc.htm.jsonl, page 80; 10-K_2025-09-30_embc.htm.jsonl, page 136; 10-Q_2026-06-30_embc.htm.jsonl, page 26; calculation C7

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Strengths that support creditors are cash conversion of 61.9% of reported EBITDA, capital expenditure of 0.9% of revenue, fixed-rate notes for 47.6% of principal, a record of voluntary prepayments of USD 245.4 million and a brand the company describes as widely recognised and international growth of 7.5%.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-K_2025-09-30_embc.htm.jsonl, page 4; 10-Q_2026-06-30_embc.htm.jsonl, page 22; 10-K_2025-09-30_embc.htm.jsonl, page 129; calculation C2; calculation C3; calculation C7

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Weaknesses that constrain creditors are United States price and volume erosion, rising net leverage of 4.67x (4.67x pro forma on net debt of USD 1,241.0 million for the dividend payable on 2026-09-15), concentration in pen needles and three distributors, negative total equity of USD -612.7 million and a single-source supplier that can end supply on a change of control.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C1; calculation C9; calculation C14

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Opportunities that could improve credit quality are generic GLP-1 co-packaging launched in Canada, Brazil and India, the Owen Mumford drug delivery platform, completion of the brand transition by the end of calendar 2026, regulatory clearance of market-appropriate pen needles and the outcome of the cost review.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Threats that could weaken credit quality are competitive bidding or price negotiation by payers, local low-cost providers aided by tariffs and buy-local preferences, once-weekly therapies, withdrawal of the receivable buyer, and revolver tests that tighten from 2028.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Scale and market position: Average. Revenue of USD 1,018.7 million over the last twelve months, a widely recognised brand and use by many insulin patients give scale, but the position is one product family under price pressure.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-09-30_embc.htm.jsonl, page 4; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C2

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Competitive advantage: Weak. Sales deductions of 34.9% of gross sales, a price effect of USD 27.4 million in nine months and entry by low-cost providers show limited pricing power despite brand and registrations.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Business diversification: Weak. Pen needles were 68.6% of revenue, the United States 46.0%, three distributors about 42% of gross sales and cannulas come from one supplier; Owen Mumford and GLP-1 co-packaging are early.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-09-30_embc.htm.jsonl, page 26; calculation C9

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Cost and capex flexibility: Average. Capital expenditure of 0.9% of revenue and a fall of USD 56.9 million in operating expenses show flexibility, but part of it is one-off and capital expenditure is already well below depreciation and amortisation.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_embc.htm.jsonl, pages 4, 34; calculation C2; calculation C10; calculation C11

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Margin stability: Weak. Gross margin fell to 58.7% from 63.5% on price and volume, and guidance implies lower fourth-quarter adjusted operating income than the third quarter.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: EX99.1_2026-06-30_embc_q32026ex-991-htm.htm.jsonl, pages 2–5; calculation C10; calculation C12

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Free cash flow stability: Average. Free cash flow of USD 164.6 million over the last twelve months is strong, but it was USD 19.9 million in fiscal 2024 and depends partly on receivable sales.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-09-30_embc.htm.jsonl, page 103; 10-Q_2026-06-30_embc.htm.jsonl, pages 4, 25; calculation C2; calculation C3

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Ability to refinance and access capital markets: Weak. Moody's and S&P cut their ratings to B3 and B in May 2026, debt is marked at 81.5% of carrying value and the extended revolver costs more, while 89.7% of principal is due in fiscal 2029 and 2030; the amend-and-extend of USD 210.0 million shows bank access remains.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_embc.htm.jsonl, pages 22, 42, 52; calculation C6; calculation C7; calculation C8; calculation C15

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Liquidity position: Average. Cash of USD 214.7 million and undrawn commitments cover fiscal 2027 maturities of USD 139.4 million, but commitments were cut to USD 310.0 million and letters of credit are not stated.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Financial policy and governance: Average. Voluntary prepayments and a dividend cut support creditors, while buybacks, a debt-funded acquisition, a combined chair and chief executive role and an unquantified class action weigh against them.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Across the nine dimensions none is assessed Strong, four are Weak and five are Average. The main supports are cash conversion and a long maturity runway; the main constraints are price erosion, concentration and refinancing pressure; the trend is negative; and the key missing datapoints are covenant definitions, agency reports, peer data and results after 2026-06-30.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Over the next twelve to twenty-four months the outlook is pressured. Management guides fiscal 2026 reported revenue down 6.1% to 4.2%, or down 10.2% to 8.8% organically at constant currency, and the implied fourth quarter is weaker than the third. The revolver commitments of USD 100.0 million due on 2027-03-31 and the covenant steps from 2028 fall in this window, so deleveraging has to start before then.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: EX99.1_2026-06-30_embc_q32026ex-991-htm.htm.jsonl, pages 4–5; 10-Q_2026-06-30_embc.htm.jsonl, page 52; calculation C12; calculation C5; calculation C6

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Over three to five years the term loan of USD 618.0 million in March 2029 and the notes of USD 700.0 million in February 2030 are the test. Tailwinds are GLP-1 co-packaging, Owen Mumford, the brand transition and any cost savings; headwinds are payer pricing, low-cost providers, once-weekly therapies and the single-source cannula supply. Each tailwind is early and unquantified, while each headwind is already visible in nine-month price and volume.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_embc.htm.jsonl, page 22; EX99.1_2026-06-30_embc_q32026ex-991-htm.htm.jsonl, page 2; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C7

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The initiating condition is that the nine-month 2026 pattern in United States pen needles continues into fiscal 2027: payers and distributors keep taking price and volume, and the receivable buyer does not increase purchases. The first operational break is net price, because concessions reach gross profit with no cost offset, and fixed manufacturing cost is then spread over fewer units. If reported EBITDA fell at the 23.9% rate that issuer-adjusted EBITDA fell in nine months 2026, last-twelve-months EBITDA would be about USD 202.3 million; on unchanged net debt of USD 1,240.4 million (USD 1,241.0 million pro forma for the dividend payable on 2026-09-15) net leverage would be 6.13x and cover on net interest expense 2.09x, against 4.67x and 2.75x now; 6.13x is above the first lien level of 4.75x, although that test is defined differently. This is an illustration at an observed rate, not a forecast, and covenant headroom under it is not established.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Liquidity would hold for a time: free cash flow would stay positive, cash and undrawn commitments are USD 584.8 million before the amendment and USD 394.8 million after it on an unchanged drawing, and the pressure points fall on known dates. The USD 100.0 million of commitments due on 2027-03-31 is the first refinancing event, the 2028 covenant steps are the first test of leverage, and the term loan in 2029 and notes in 2030 follow with debt already marked at 81.5% of carrying value. Management's levers are to stop buybacks, keep the dividend at USD 0.01 a share, direct cash to voluntary prepayments as it did in fiscal 2025, use the cost review and rely on receivable sales, but capital expenditure is already low, so little room remains there. Resilience looks sufficient to avoid a liquidity crisis within twelve months on the evidence supplied, and not sufficient to meet a first lien limit of 3.75x in 2028 without an EBITDA recovery or large debt reduction. Observable triggers are fourth-quarter fiscal 2026 results, the pace of the United States decline, revolver drawings and buyback pace.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Overall, Embecta presents a weak business profile supported by a brand the company calls widely recognised, low capital intensity and cash conversion of 61.9% in the last twelve months, but credit quality is constrained by United States price and volume erosion, net leverage of 4.67x (4.67x pro forma on net debt of USD 1,241.0 million for the dividend payable on 2026-09-15) and a policy tilt toward buybacks and acquisition. Cash-flow durability appears adequate rather than strong because free cash flow was volatile before the last year and depends in part on receivable sales. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on stabilising United States earnings before the revolver commitments of USD 100.0 million due on 2027-03-31 are addressed and before USD 1,318.0 million falls due in fiscal 2029 and 2030. The primary downside path is continued price and volume erosion that lifts leverage into tightening covenants while the debt is already marked at 81.5% of carrying value and rated B3 by Moody's and B by S&P. Further analysis would need the executed covenant definitions and compliance figures, the fiscal 2026 annual results, agency reports and outlooks, peer data and the split of the revolver drawing. Fundamental credit completed. Top risk: continued United States pen needle price and volume erosion while leverage rises.
